question: Should the QA owner accept the new strict two-part, one-feature/one-coverage-ID contract and the associated `smoke-ci` semantic narrowing once the exact-head checks are terminal?
rationale: This is not a mechanical defect decision: it changes the taxonomy and profile meaning that QA automation uses to represent product evidence, and the PR is protected by member/maintainer signals.

options.title: Accept the QA contract change
options.body: Confirm that one globally unique `surface.feature` ID per atomic feature and the reduced `smoke-ci` category set are the intended authoritative reporting model after checks complete.

options.title: Request a narrower taxonomy proposal
options.body: Keep the existing coverage model and ask for a separately reviewed proposal that limits semantic remapping to the specific collision cases.

options.title: Pause for CI resolution
options.body: Hold the semantic decision until the failed compact lane is explained or fixed and the remaining QA/compact checks reach terminal conclusions.

recommendation.title: Accept the QA contract change
recommendation.body: Confirm that one globally unique `surface.feature` ID per atomic feature and the reduced `smoke-ci` category set are the intended authoritative reporting model after checks complete.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the identified current contributor for the QA taxonomy model and can provide the mapping rationale; final acceptance should come from the relevant QA code owner.
